questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

She said, "Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate."

options.text: She said that Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak was slipping when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak has slipped when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak had slipped when he was trying to skate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e *She said that Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25cf3443523bdade9b54eae0f44214d7fb9974cacdd0708b2812ee08d9a34014.png] **__Explanation:__**

__
 
• While changing direct speech into indirect speech change in the tense will not occur when the time clause is mentioned ('when')
 
• Reporting speech and reported speech are joined with that if the given sentence is a simple sentence.
 
• These rules are followed in option 1) making it the correct answer.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In complex sentences, the past simple and past continuous may remain unchanged if the temporal relationship between the events in the clauses is clear from the context. Examples: 
 
 
• Bill: I was reading a book when I heard the crash.

 Bill said that he was reading a book when he heard the crash.
 
• John: When I got home, I went to bed straight away.

 John told me that when he got home he went to bed straight away.

He said to me, “I go for a walk daily.”

options.text: He told me that he went for a walk daily.
He told me that he goes for a walk daily.
He told me that he daily went for a walk.
He told me that he had gone for a walk daily.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He told me that he goes for a walk daily.'**

• whereas 'said to' will change into 'told' but the tense in the reported speech will not change because the time reference is given that denotes habitual action.
 
• *So the correct indirect speech is-* He told me that he goes for a walk daily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an **in**direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting indirect speech into direct speech__:​
 __
 
• The commas and inverted commas are added.
 
• The third person 'he' will be changed into the second person 'you'.
 
• The past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (reached) + Object' will be changed into the present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (reach) + Object'.
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as- option 3*.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

He says, “I am a little bit afraid.”

options.text: He was a little bit afraid, he said
He said he was afraid
He says that he is a little bit afraid
He says that he was a little bit afraid

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3. **

In Direct speech, the actual words of the speaker are quoted within quotation marks.

In Indirect speech, we report someone else’s words in our own words.

When we change the speech from Direct to Indirect, we do not use the quotation marks. Also, we use 'that' before the Indirect statement. We make suitable changes in tenses as well.

The most important point to be noted here is that if the reporting verb is in the present tense, the tenses of the verbs in the reported speech remain unchanged. 

Since the reporting verb is 'says', the first person singular verb 'am' in the direct speech becomes 'is' in the third person singular.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in**** ****Indirect/Direct Speech.** 

“Are you going to eat with us?” he asked.

options.text: He asked me if I was going to eat with them.
He asked whether he was going to eat with them.
He inquired whether I am going to eat or not.
She asked me if he was going to eat with them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **He asked me if I was going to eat with them. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

To change the sentence from **Direct** to **Indirect **we should:

 
• Make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the reported speech is an interrogative sentence we follow these steps-
 
 
• The reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'asked'.
 
• Connector 'if' or 'whether' is used in place of commas.
 
• Change the sentence, given in the reported speech, from interrogative to assertive.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed accordingly.(in above sentence- 'are' changes into 'was')
 
• Personal Pronouns of reported speech are changed as per the subject and object of reporting verb. Here, the second person- 'You' will change into **'I'** as per object - **'me' (hidden).**
 
 

**Thus the correct answer is Option 1**

questions.question:
**Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence.**

Dhiraj said that he had been to Goa the previous year also.

options.text: Dhiraj said, “I had been to Goa the previous year also.”
Dhiraj said, “He has been to Goa the previous year also.”
Dhiraj told, “I went to Goa the last year also.”
Dhiraj said, “I have been to Goa last year also.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **Dhiraj said, “I have been to Goa last year also.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​​

__
 
• Let's look at the **steps** to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:

 
 
• When the indirect speech is in the assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
• The connector 'that' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas.
 
• The pronoun 'he' is replaced by 'I' accordingly.​
 
• The past perfect continuous tense will be changed to the present perfect continuous tense in direct speech resulting in the following changes:
 
 
• had been- have been.​
 
 
 
• Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (the previous year-last year)
 
 
 
• ​At last, line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get - Dhiraj said, “I have been to Goa last year also.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If **reported verb is in Past Tense,** reported speech will change from **Present Perfect Continuous Tense to Past Perfect Continuous Tense**
 
• **Example:- **
 
 
• He said, “It have been snowing all night.” :-** ****He said that it had been snowing all night.**
 
• Uncle said, “I have been working very hard.” :- **Uncle said that he had been working very hard.**
